description: Combine 805f3d's four-warp prepack/stationary pipeline with 0ffeee's 640-thread 296-CTA persistent launch. Remove near-update per-thread projected[16] state via lane-striped or shared warpgroup compact-WY transforms, then bracket 640/768/1024 threads. Target a two-resident-CTA register footprint with no local spills while preserving the full last-128 tcgen05 atom and one TMEM allocation per persistent CTA.

The first 1024-thread shared rank-8 compact-WY rewrite built, but validation stopped before GPU execution because its comment used the banned word 'stream'. No numerical checks or benchmark ran; the implementation must be reapplied with guard-safe wording.

Replaced the near-update per-lane projected[16] array with two rank-8 projection passes. Each warp stores reduced W and lane-striped triangular Z coefficients in a private shared slot, then consumes shared broadcasts for the row update. Full validation/guards passed at 1024 threads. Dense n512 measured 16187.277 us versus parent 16062.250 us (+0.78%); full geomean was 1429.468 versus 1424.239 amid untouched-route variance. This removes the long-lived 16-coefficient state for the lower-thread residency trials.

Removed the shared Z vector and broadcast one transformed coefficient from lanes 0-15, but validation hung in the dense differential guard and was terminated after 346 seconds. The final 16-row panel has only lanes 0-15 in the row loop while the shuffle used FULL, producing an invalid synchronization mask. No benchmark ran.

Removed the second shared Z vector: lanes 0-15 retained one transformed coefficient and row updates fetched them with active-mask warp shuffles. Full validation/guards passed after correcting the final half-warp mask. Dense n512 regressed from the shared-Z trial's 16187.277 to 18339.474 us; geomean was 1445.287. Sixteen shuffles per row are substantially more expensive than shared broadcasts, despite the smaller state footprint.

Combined the shared-Z rank-8 near update with a 640-thread launch, one reusable correction A stage, and a 296-CTA persistent matrix loop retaining one TMEM allocation. Full validation and all guards passed. Dense n512 regressed from parent 16062.250 to 20065.232 us (+24.92%); full geomean was 1452.150. Two-resident occupancy and reduced projection state did not offset lower per-matrix warp parallelism, extra correction-stage barriers, and the unavoidable third scheduling wave for batch 640.

Focused NCU of the full-valid 640-thread persistent commit failed before kernel launch because the profiler sudo child could load libnvrtc.so.13 but not the venv-provided libnvrtc-builtins.so.13.0. This is a profiler environment failure; retrying the unchanged commit with the cu13 library directory explicitly forwarded.

Reduced each near-column projection from two rank-8 accumulator passes to four rank-4 passes to lower live registers under the 640-thread two-CTA launch bound. Full validation and all guards passed, but dense n512 regressed from rank-8 20065.232 to 23365.113 us (+16.45%) and geomean to 1471.030. Re-reading each target column four times costs far more than the measured 469 KB launch-wide spill traffic; retain rank-8 for the thread-count bracket.

Bracketed the rank-8 shared-Z persistent fusion at 768 threads/24 warps while retaining a 296-CTA grid, two-block launch bound, one TMEM allocation per CTA, and a 115200-byte shared footprint. Full validation and all guards passed. Dense n512 regressed from the 640-thread trial's 20065.232 to 21441.280 us (+6.86%); geomean was 1460.133. Four additional near-update warps do not repay the tighter register ceiling and larger CTA barrier cohort.

Completed the thread bracket at 1024 threads/32 warps with a one-block launch bound, 296 persistent CTAs, one TMEM allocation per CTA, rank-8 shared-Z near updates, and the one-A-stage correction workspace. Full validation and all guards passed. Dense n512 improved from 768-thread 21441.280 to 16263.597 us but remained 1.25% behind parent 16062.250; geomean was 1428.364. The delayed second half of a 296-CTA grid still leaves a five-matrix critical path on 148 SMs.

Reduced the 1024-thread persistent grid from 296 to one CTA per SM (148), so each CTA reuses one TMEM allocation across four or five matrices. Full validation and all guards passed. Dense n512 was neutral/slightly worse at 16282.176 versus 16263.597 us (+0.11%); geomean was 1430.152 amid broader-route variance. Allocation amortization is negligible and the five-matrix critical depth is unchanged; the 296-CTA commit remains the best persistent bracket point.

Replaced rank-8 near projection arrays with a lane-striped pair scheme: each lane keeps one coefficient, a 32 KiB row-major shared V view avoids bank-conflicted coefficient reads, and target-column rows load once before shuffle exchange. Restored the faster 296-CTA persistent grid. Full validation and all guards passed. Dense n512 regressed from the rank-8 296-CTA trial's 16263.597 to 21574.243 us (+32.66%); geomean was 1460.813. Per-tile shuffle exchange and V staging overwhelm the smaller live state and halved target-column loads.

Completed the requested 805f3d plus 0ffeee combination and 640/768/1024 bracket, with one TMEM allocation per persistent CTA, full last-128 tcgen05 stationary atom, reduced correction workspace, and full validation on every successful source trial. Best new nonpersistent state rewrite is ca953d297: shared-Z rank-8 projection removes projected[16] and measures 16187.277 us dense versus parent 16062.250 (+0.78%). Best true persistent combination is 522b6a89d at 1024 threads, 296 CTAs: dense 16263.597 us, geomean 1428.364, 1.25% behind parent. The two-resident candidates were much slower: 640 threads 20065.232 us and 768 threads 21441.280 us. NCU verified the 640 build really has two resident CTAs, 48 regs/thread, 62.5% theoretical and about 48% achieved occupancy, but still 469 KB spill requests, 68.3% no-eligible cycles, and large barrier/scoreboard stalls. Rank-4 projection eliminated live accumulators at the cost of repeated target reads and regressed to 23365.113 us. A lane-striped paired-lane projection with row-major shared V loaded each target row once but regressed to 21574.243 us; NCU showed 64 regs/thread, 50% achieved occupancy, and 9.73 MB spills versus 6.54 MB for the rank-8 1024 final profile, so its unrolled shuffle network increased pressure. A 148-CTA grid was neutral/slower at 16282.176 us. Profiles are in autocuda/profiles/2026-07-06-18-24-02. Parent 805f3d remains the dense winner. Most promising remaining direction is true warp-specialized dynamic register redistribution (setmaxnreg) or call-graph isolation so the four stationary tcgen x16 tuple warps can borrow registers without imposing their peak on the 28 near-update warps; retain rank-8 shared broadcasts and avoid extra global passes or per-tile shuffle exchange. Direct tcgen05 consumption of panel_v without the B prepack remains a second direction. No leaderboard submission was made, as instructed.
